message: The protected-branch safety gate must be in force: the protected branch must require a pull request, require the engine checks to pass on a branch brought up to date with the base first (freshness — so a check that passed against an older base cannot merge stale), require unresolved review conversations to be resolved, and block force-pushes and deletion. This is the gate that lets a non-engineer walk away trusting that nothing reaches the protected branch unchecked, and that a green check means the actual merge candidate is green. In CI this is verified against the live branch ruleset; on your own machine it reports 'not checked here' because it has no access token, which is expected. If it reports the gate is not in force — including that a change could merge without first being brought up to date with the base — apply the protected-branch ruleset using the setup recipe; if you maintain your own branch rule, turn on 'Require branches to be up to date before merging' to close the freshness gap yourself. With freshness on, an advance of the base branch means a green pull request needs a routine branch update and re-check before it can merge — that is normal churn, not a conflict; a genuine conflict is only when that update cannot apply cleanly and needs a manual rebase. A merge queue, offered where GitHub supports one, removes the routine churn by proving the integration candidate for you.
